transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Schiavone.
Lawmakers are frustrated over the administration's refusal to send hundreds of millions of dollars
allocated by Congress out to its intended recipients.
The maneuver called a pocket rescission is illegal, according to the nonpartisan watchdog
agency, the Government Accountability Office, NPR Congressional reporter Eric McDaniel has
more.
That's the power of the purse, they get to decide where and how money is spent.
But for the second year in a row, the president is making some of those decisions himself.
He withheld $800 million from programs that touch immigrant services, racial and sexual
minority work, and climate change programs, and appropriators on the Hill are upset.
Republican Susan Collins of Maine says this is the most recent attempt by the White House
to undermine Congress's constitutional powers.
Her Democratic counterpart, Patty Murray of Washington, called it theft, and the top Democrat
on the House Budget Committee, Brenda Boyle, says, "Donald Trump knows he can't get these
cuts through Congress, so he is illegally making them through the back door."
Eric McDaniel, NPR News in Washington.
Diesel prices have slipped a little, but the war in Iran continues to strain fuel supplies,
and PR's Windsor-Johnson reports the concern now is how long higher costs could keep working
their way into household bills.
Farmers in many parts of the country are still paying much more to run combines, tractors
and trucks during the fall harvest.
Higher fuel costs can move through the food supply chain, and the pressure may last.
Diesel and home heating oil draw on the same tight fuel supply as winter approaches.
Some shipping costs are set by contractors, so shoppers may not see the full effect right
away.
U.S. fuel inventories are low, leaving little cushion if supplies are disrupted again.
That's why a modest drop in diesel prices offers only limited relief.
The Trump administration has discussed expanding U.S. refining capacity but has not announced
an immediate measure to lower prices.
Windsor-Johnson, NPR News.
A hurricane watch has been lifted for Hawaii's Big Island.
Local officials are now taking stock of the storm's aftermath.
NPR's Juliana Kim reports from the island of Oahu.
The impacts from Hurricane Nolo are beginning to ease, including threats of flooding and
a storm surge that's according to the National Hurricane Center.
Nolo dumped several inches of rain across the Big Island on Saturday, which led to flooding
on a number of roads.
On Sunday morning, thousands were without power on Big Island and Maui.
Nolo remains just south of the Hawaiian Islands and is expected to strengthen again into a
major hurricane over the next 24 hours before weakening later in the week.
Juliana Kim, NPR News, Honolulu.
Drenching rains continued to saturate shorelines in the northeastern U.S. today.
Another round of flooding hit low-lying areas of New York and New Jersey and led to many
power outages traveled by land and air have been disrupted throughout the weekend.
This is NPR.
In a visit to Lourdes, France today, Pope Leo the 14th spoke out against legislative
efforts in France and elsewhere to allow adults with incurable illnesses to receive lethal
medications, declaring those in extreme pain have an inherent dignity that no law can eliminate.
A hundred fifty thousand people, many in wheelchairs, attended the mass led by the Pope.
The zoo in Atlanta is welcoming two new giant pandas.
They arrived from China this morning, part of a new agreement between the U.S. and Chinese
governments.
The loan of pandas is part of China's global diplomacy program.
NPR's Kristin Wright has more.
Male panda ping-ping, who's six, and female fu-shuang, who's five, flew in on Boeing's
FedEx Panda Express jet.
The giant pandas will stay in quarantine for about a month in Zoo Atlanta's new panda
complex before they're introduced to the public on a date to be announced later.
Ping-ping and fu-shuang are in Atlanta for 10 years, through a new conservation agreement
between the zoo and the China Wildlife Conservation Association.
China's President Xi Jinping officially confirmed the pandas would soon arrive during his visit
to Washington last week.
Zoo Atlanta is one of three zoos in the U.S. with pandas on loan from China.
Once in danger, they're now classified as vulnerable species.
Kristin Wright, NPR News.
President Trump attended the President's Cup Golf Tournament in Medina, Illinois, today,
the fourth time this year for Trump to be at a golf tournament.
He says the PGA Tour was nice enough to name him honorary chairman.
It's a traditional role offered to every head of state in the country that is hosting the
golf tournament.
I'm Louise Schiavone, NPR News, Washington.

topics.text: Administration withholds $800 million from immigrant services, minority programs, climate change via pocket rescission
War in Iran strains fuel supplies; diesel prices slip but higher costs may persist in household bills
Hurricane Nolo impacts ease for Hawaii's Big Island; storm expected to strengthen again before weakening
Drenching rains cause flooding in northeastern U.S., disrupting travel in New York and New Jersey
Pope Leo the 14th speaks against euthanasia legislation during visit to Lourdes, France; 150,000 attend mass
Giant pandas Ping-ping and Fu-shuang arrive at Zoo Atlanta from China on 10-year loan agreement
